reference.title: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower the dumbbells, exhale as you press them up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: Add reps up to the top of the range, then move to the next dumbbell (usually 1-2.5 kg per hand).

cues.text: Set the back pad to 30 degrees, glutes in the crease, upper back and head on the pad, feet planted; dumbbells up over the upper chest with the palms facing each other.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells beside the upper chest, elbows tucked about 30 degrees from your sides, forearms vertical.
Handles parallel to the body beside the chest, upper arms just below the pad line; no bounce.
Breathe out and press straight up over the shoulders, palms still facing each other.
Arms straight but not locked, dumbbells a few centimetres apart, shoulder blades still back on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the palms turn forward as you press
mistakes.fix: Keep the handles parallel to your body (palms facing) from bottom to top.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring out like a regular press
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tucked about 30 degrees from the sides; the neutral grip is meant to keep them close.
Use a 30-45 degree incline; steeper turns it into a shoulder press (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
Sit back into the crease and keep the feet planted.

mistakes.mistake: Banging the dumbbells together at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop with them a few centimetres apart over the shoulders.

kinematics.norm: Back pad at 30 degrees (the angle that gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity in Rodríguez-Ridao 2020; Lauver 2016 also recommends 30 degrees); 30-45 degrees is common for the incline hammer press (clinical opinion)
Neutral (palms facing each other) throughout (clinical opinion; the neutral grip shifted activity toward the clavicular pectoralis in a seated press, Muyor 2023)
Arms straight but not locked at the top; dumbbells beside the chest at the bottom with the elbows roughly 90-110 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 20-40 degrees from the body, closer than a pronated press (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020 (head, shoulders and hips on the bench)
Controlled: about 2 s down and 1-2 s up; Rodríguez-Ridao 2020 used 2 s down and 2 s up at 60% of 1RM

sources.title: GymVisual #032112, Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press, video (movement reference)

Rodríguez-Ridao, Antequera-Vique, Martín-Fuentes and Muyor 2020, effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339; PMC7579505)
Lauver, Cayot and Scheuermann, influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise (Eur J Sport Sci, 2016; PubMed 25799093)

Muyor, Rodríguez-Ridao and Oliva-Lozano 2023, comparison of muscle activity between the horizontal bench press and the seated chest press exercises using several grips (J Hum Kinet 87:23-34; doi 10.5114/jhk/161468)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells on the thighs, then lie back and kick them up one knee at a time; at the end of the set bring them back to the thighs or lower them to the floor beside the bench rather than dropping them (clinical opinion).
Shoulder discomfort in the regular press: the neutral grip with tucked elbows is often more comfortable; keep the range pain-free (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower the bench to 15-30 degrees if the shoulders take over.
Shorten the range at the bottom if the front of the shoulder is uncomfortable.
progressions: Slower lowering (3-4 s) with a 1 s pause.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher, biased toward the upper (clavicular) fibres by the incline: 30 degrees gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity in pressing (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, barbell). In a seated chest press the neutral grip gave more clavicular activity than a wide pronated barbell grip (Muyor 2023).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher, biased toward the upper (clavicular) fibres by the incline: 30 degrees gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity in pressing (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, barbell). In a seated chest press the neutral grip gave more clavicular activity than a wide pronated barbell grip (Muyor 2023).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder; with the elbows tucked by the neutral grip the press is more of a forward (flexion) push, and the deltoid works harder as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder; with the elbows tucked by the neutral grip the press is more of a forward (flexion) push, and the deltoid works harder as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows; triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows; triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Works as a stabiliser: biceps activity rose with the stability demand, highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Works as a stabiliser: biceps activity rose with the stability demand, highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the seat.

phases.label: Arms straight over the upper chest
